speaker: a014

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Roan's dead and Fina's got nobody but you and me now — that's not nothing, that's a wall we didn't have yesterday. I want you feeding her steady and keeping her close, and if anyone in this village starts counting her food out loud the way Vela counted it last year, you tell me before you tell them.

speaker: a013
text: Roan's death sat on me harder than I expected, and I'm still sorting out whether that means Fina leans on us more now or whether she learns to stand harder — I think it's both, and I think we need to let her decide which before we start building walls around her without asking. What I need from you this year is plain: the pile's at six and you've already taken two, and I need to know if you're done or if you're counting on more, because Fina's twenty food draws eyes and I won't be the last person in this village to notice that you're sitting light.

speaker: a001
text: I'm done at two — I'm not going to sit on a pile while Fina draws every eye in the village and I look like I'm waiting to take from her. What I need from you is simple: keep some of that twenty quiet, give a little here and there so nobody can point at one number and say that's the target, and make sure she understands that generosity this year is cheaper than a fight.

speaker: a013
text: Twenty is already out there — Vela named it in a room last year and half this village was listening, so the quiet ship has sailed. What I can do is make sure the number people are counting by year's end is smaller, and I'll start with Sela and Zinn because food that moves to blood doesn't look like weakness, it looks like family. But Bram, I need you to hear this plainly: if Mako decides Fina's twenty is worth the trouble before we've scattered enough of it, two food and fifty-eight strength isn't the wall she needs.

speaker: a001
text: You're right that I'm not the wall she needs — so tell me who is, because if Mako moves on Fina this year, I need to know before it happens which names in this village will stand up and which ones will wait to see who wins. Vela and Esa made me a promise in that room, and I need to know if that promise still has teeth with Taric and Roan both in the ground.

speaker: a013
text: Vela and Esa both made that promise when Taric was standing beside them and Roan was alive to back it — two bodies in the ground changes the math on what a promise costs to keep, so I'd test it small before you count on it large. The name I actually trust to stand when Mako moves is Zinn, because she's been feeding me all year with her father watching, and a woman who does that has already paid a cost. Get me a quiet hour with Kael before the pile empties, because he's got one food and nothing to lose, and a man with nothing to lose is either dangerous or useful and I'd rather find out which before Mako does.

speaker: a001
text: Kael's a good read — one food at fifty-five means he's already decided this year is about survival, not positioning, and a man in that place will take any hand that's offered. Go to him before he goes to Mako, because Mako will make the same calculation I would and he'll move first. I'll stay close to Fina and keep my mouth shut until you tell me what Kael said.

speaker: a013
text: Before I go to Kael, I want to know one thing you haven't told me yet — Vela's been feeding you for years and she's been quiet this morning, and a woman who goes quiet after she's been loud is either finished or planning, and I need to know which one you think it is.

speaker: a001
text: Vela's fifty-five and she watched Taric die — a woman that age with that much history doesn't go quiet because she's done, she goes quiet because she's deciding something she hasn't said yet. I don't know which way she's deciding, and that's what bothers me. Get to Kael first, but don't leave Vela's door dark — I want you to know what she's sitting on before she opens it herself.

speaker: a013
text: Vela's door I'll knock before sundown — but Bram, hear me: if she's planning something that turns away from us, I need you to already know which direction you'll move, because I won't be the one standing in the open holding a story about family loyalty while you're still deciding. Go to Fina now, stay close, and don't tell her anything about Kael or Vela until I'm back.

speaker: a001
text: Understood — I'll go to Fina now and I won't say a word about Kael or Vela. But if you get to Vela's door and she's already moved toward Mako, don't knock — come straight to me, because that changes everything I need to decide before dark.

speaker: a013
text: One more thing before you go — Zinn took three from the pile this morning, which is more than she needed and more than I'd expect from a woman sitting light last year, and I want to know if Mako put food in her hands before the pile opened or if she's just eating for herself now.

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, Roan's gone and the pile's got four left and I haven't touched it yet — tell me your food count right now, because you're forty-eight and I am not going to let you run thin while Zinn's sitting on three and Nessa's got sixteen. After that I want to talk about Vela, because we never finished that conversation and a woman who was waking up to Bram a year ago is either all the way awake by now or she's been swallowed back into his circle, and I need to know which before this year moves any further.

speaker: a009
text: Four food, Dell — and two satiation, which means I eat before anything else leaves my hands, same as I promised you. Vela I can't read clean yet; she named Bram's name herself in that circle last year, which was something, but she kept feeding him right through it, and a woman who wakes up and still opens her hand is either not all the way awake or she's paying a debt she hasn't told us about. I want to hear her say his name again this year, unprompted, before I count her as anything more than a useful neighbor.

speaker: a011
text: Four's enough to keep you breathing but it's not enough to keep me easy — take two of mine before this day closes, because I've got eight and Ryn running thin is a problem I can fix right now. On Vela: if she doesn't say his name before the pile's settled this year, I'm done waiting on her to wake up all the way; a useful neighbor who keeps feeding the man we're all watching is still feeding the man we're all watching.

speaker: a009
text: I'll take the two, Dell, and I won't argue about it — but I want us to talk about Fina before the day closes, because Roan's gone and she's got twenty food and no father standing beside her anymore, and that's the number that changes everything about how this year runs.

speaker: a011
text: Twenty food and no father is a woman who's about to learn very fast who counts her as kin and who counts her as a larder — and I want to be the first name she hears, not Bram's, not Mako's. She's twenty-four and strong enough to matter in a fight, and if she's half as sharp as Nessa she already knows the number on her back is dangerous. What do you know about how she and Nessa read each other, because that's the thread I'd pull first.

speaker: a009
text: Nessa's been feeding Fina since before Roan was gone — food moving that direction through most of last year, which means either Nessa already counts her as someone worth protecting or she's been building a claim on her loyalty, and either way Fina knows Nessa's name better than she knows ours. That's the thread I'd pull second; the first one I'd pull is going to Fina directly, today, before anyone else does, and letting her see a woman who's been watching this village longer than she's been alive and isn't trying to count her food.

speaker: a011
text: Then I'm going to Fina before the pile settles — but I want you to come with me, because a woman who just lost her father doesn't need one face, she needs two, and yours carries something mine doesn't yet. We'll walk in talking about Roan, not about her food, and let her tell us what she's afraid of before we say anything about what we can offer.

speaker: a009
text: I'll go with you, and I won't say Roan's name like a strategy — I'll say it because I watched him stand more times than most men here and I meant it when I counted him as solid. Let Fina do the talking first; grief tells you more about a person than anything they'd say when they're composed. If she cries, we sit with her; if she's already counting, we count with her and let her see we're not surprised.

speaker: a011
text: Before we walk through Fina's door, I want to say one thing out loud that I've been carrying quiet: Kael's sitting on one food and fifty-five years, and nobody's feeding him, and a man who's been solid in this village that long doesn't deserve to starve in the background while we're all watching Fina's number. If he's still breathing when we come back from Fina, I want to give him something.

speaker: a009
text: Kael's been quiet so long this village has started forgetting he's counting too — and a man who's been around that long has seen every shape trouble comes in before anyone else names it. Give him something, and give it where people can see you do it, because generosity toward the old ones says something about who you are before you've had to prove it the hard way. We'll go to Fina first, then Kael, and we'll let the day do the rest.

speaker: a011
text: One more thing before we walk — the pile still has four and I haven't taken from it yet, and I want you to know I'm leaving it for whoever's thinner than I am, because eight food and two satiation means I can afford that choice and I want this village to see me make it.

speaker: a009
text: That's the right choice, and I'll say so to anyone who asks me why the pile still had food in it when we walked away — it'll mean more coming from someone who isn't you. Go let them see it, and then we find Fina.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Roan's gone and the pile's already empty — so I want to know, right now, between the three of us: Esa, are you still feeding Bram, and Vela, are you still feeding Bram, because if both of you are pouring food into that man's household I need to understand what you think you're buying with it.

speaker: a003
text: Kael, I gave him food because Taric is gone and I'm thirty-three strength standing alone — Bram's got Nessa and Fina's blood in this village and that makes him the man most likely to move if someone comes at me. I know it only runs one direction and I know what that costs me.

speaker: a002
text: I stopped feeding Bram after year nine — I gave him six food across that season and I watched every piece of it flow straight into Nessa's hands, which isn't nothing, but it isn't protection either. What I'm buying now, if I'm buying anything, is Nessa and Fina staying friendly when Mako decides the arithmetic suits him, and I need to know whether you two see the same threat I do or whether I'm the only one who's been counting.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, you're not the only one counting — Mako's got two bloodlines in this village and four food in hand and he hasn't moved yet, which means he's waiting on something, and I want to know what. Kael, the question that keeps me awake isn't whether Mako moves, it's whether Dell moves with him, because Dell's been filling Ryn's hands all year and Ryn's never told this circle what she said when she went to talk to her.

speaker: a002
text: Dell gave me one food this year, which I did not ask for and do not know how to read — a woman who feeds Ryn like clockwork and then turns and drops something in my hands is either buying goodwill from every direction or she's already decided which way she's leaning and wants to be remembered kindly when it settles. Kael, you've been in rooms with Dell that I haven't — does she move with Mako, or does she move for herself?

speaker: a003
text: Kael, answer Vela's question — but while you're thinking, I'll say the thing I've been holding: Dell gave Ryn seven food this year and gave Vela one, and that's not goodwill spread evenly, that's a hierarchy, and Ryn sits at the top of it. Whatever Dell is, she's not neutral.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, you've been in this village since the beginning and you haven't answered the question twice now, which is its own answer — so I'll say what I think you're holding: you know something about Dell and Mako that you don't want to name in front of Esa and me, and I'd rather you said it plain and let us decide what to do with it than carry it alone until the moment passes.

speaker: a003
text: Kael, Vela's right and I'll say it harder: you've pulled us into this room three times now and asked questions you already know the answers to, and the only reason a man does that is because he wants witnesses, not information — so whatever you're carrying about Dell and Mako, say it now, because I've got four food and thirty-three strength and I need to know whether what's coming has two legs or three.

speaker: a004
text: What I'm carrying isn't a secret — it's an absence. I don't have a room with Dell, I've never been in one, and that's what I was holding: Mako has roots through three women in this village and I have zero, and a man sitting on that kind of bloodline doesn't need to move this year or next year, he just needs everyone else to stay isolated until the arithmetic does the work for him. The question I want answered before this year closes isn't Dell's loyalty — it's whether the two of you are willing to stand as something visible enough that Mako has to count you before he counts against you.
